label: Bible Study
prompt: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a _____ the foal of an ass.
verse: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.
note: Fulfilled on Palm Sunday — Matthew and John both quote it as Jesus rides into Jerusalem.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye _____.
verse: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
note: Let God's peace rule in your heart, Paul says — and, as a fine finishing touch, be thankful.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there _____ round about him a light from heaven:
verse: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
note: On the Damascus road a light from heaven 'shined' round about Saul — the KJV doesn't say shone.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Now therefore give me this _____, whereof the LORD spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the LORD will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the LORD said.
verse: Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the LORD will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the LORD said.
note: Caleb at 85 asks for the hardest hill country, giants included — the faithful spy hadn't retired.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited _____, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
verse: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
note: 'Whited sepulchres' — tombs painted bright white: gleaming outside, dead men's bones within. Jesus' sharpest woe.
